rulings.evidence: Small creamer potatoes are their own bagged SKU priced well above bulk russets, and no commodity claims them though today's captures carry them; sweet-potatoes is a different food.
An unqualified oregano measured in teaspoons for a dry rub is the dried jar, matching the 2026-08-26 'ground oregano' ruling; board 7 of 7. Fresh would be a different price and gram weight.
Two distinct pantry foods on one unsplittable line, so no single bid can carry it - the 2026-08-26 precedent. Pantry-static pricing at 3 pinches is safe.
Same ruling as the Mediterranean line: one pint clamshell of small tomatoes at the same price class as cherry; the board's `grapes` match is fruit.

rulings.raw: 2 boneless, skinless chicken breasts (about 1.3 lbs. total) ($3.89)
rulings.evidence: Exact vocabulary row Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast [chicken-breast], board 7 of 7; the source states 1.3 lb total, so no each-weight assumption is needed.
Same-form vocabulary row Basil Pesto [pesto] and a live board id at 5 of 7 - a reuse. 1/4 cup jarred pesto is 64 g.
Water-packed fresh ball is a different SKU and price class from low-moisture shredded, and reduced-fat or fat-free mozzarella are different products; no commodity claims it, captures do.
spring-mix is a live board id at 7 of 7 - a reuse, only a vocabulary name row is missing. The FDC shelf returned spring wheat and scallions, a keyword miss.
caesar-dressing is a live board id (6 of 7) - a reuse; ranch is a different dressing, so no bridge to ranch-dressing.
